subject: POC observability & success criteria — Redwood x Trialsight
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@trialsight.com>, Trialsight Engineering <eng@trialsight.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC observability & success criteria — Redwood x Trialsight

Hi Elaine,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great context on Trialsight's inference workloads and the evaluation priorities. Quick recap and a proposed observability-first POC plan so engineering can size and we can sync expectations: 

Summary of ask from your team:
- 2-week functional trial against your n-gram reranking pipeline (~1.5k qps peak, average 150 qps).
- Measure latency P95/P99, token-level cost, and failure modes under burst traffic.
- Verify log export + tracing into your infra for root-cause analysis.

Proposed POC observability deliverables (high level):
- Dashboards: P95/P99 latency by model + request rate, tokens/op, token-cost breakdown, error rate by model + endpoint.
- Tracing: end-to-end spans linking client request → routing → GPU worker → model inference; sample spans for cache hits/misses.
- Logs: structured request+response metadata exported to your S3 (or S3-compatible) bucket and forwarded to your Splunk/Grafana Loki.
- Alerts/SLIs: latency SLOs, error-rate thresholds, and sudden token-cost spikes.

Success criteria (suggested, please confirm):
1) P95 latency <= 220ms for baseline model under steady-state 150 qps.
2) No more than 1% request error rate during 24h soak at expected peak.
3) Traces show end-to-end parent span for 95% of sampled requests; ability to correlate with logs within 1 minute.
4) Token-cost per 1k tokens within agreed budget (we'll add numbers once you confirm target).

Next steps I propose:
- Share an observability checklist + instrumentation snippet (attached).
- Quick engineering sync (30m) to confirm log export path and permissions.
- Agree on ownership and kickoff date.

I've attached a lightweight POC checklist and an initial SLA draft for your review. Can we do a short sync on Thursday 3/12?

Thanks,

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai

Attachments: poc-observability-checklist.xlsx, redwood-poc-sla-draft.pdf

From: Elaine Park <elaine@trialsight.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Trialsight Engineering <eng@trialsight.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC observability & success criteria — Redwood x Trialsight

Thanks, Sergio — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Log export: we prefer S3 + lifecycle rules. Can Redwood push structured logs directly, or do you require us to pull? We need a short README for auth and partitioning.
- Dashboards: we use Grafana (hosted) and would like a JSON export to import. Can you provide a starter dashboard with the core panels you listed?
- Tracing: we use OpenTelemetry. Are you able to emit spans in OTLP/Jaeger format?

Timeline constraint: we have a small procurement window next week and would like to start the POC the week of 3/16. Procurement may need an invoice and a one-page SOW.

Assigning Kyle Morgan (copied) as our eng lead — he will coordinate access. Also looping in security if we need to exchange a minimal security checklist.

Elaine Park
VP, Product
Trialsight
elaine@trialsight.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC observability & success criteria — Redwood x Trialsight (instrumentation notes)

Sergio / Camila — quick technical notes to support the ask. Copying Laura for rollout implications.

1) Logs: Redwood can push structured JSON records to an S3-compatible endpoint using signed PUTs; we also support publishing to an internal forwarder if Trialsight prefers to pull. We'll provide a small Lambda example for partitioning by day and model.

2) Traces: we emit OTLP-compatible spans. For the POC we recommend sampling at 10% globally and 100% for error traces. We can provide a Jaeger/OTLP collector container and an example collector config.

3) Dashboards: we'll supply a Grafana JSON with panels for:
   - request_rate (per endpoint),
   - latency_histogram,
   - p95_p99_time_series,
   - token_cost_breakdown,
   - kv_cache_hit_rate (if caching is enabled),
   - worker_gpu_utilization.

4) Alerts / SLIs: suggested alerting rules and example Prometheus expressions are included in the attached tracing guide (redwood-poc-tracing-guide.md). Example thresholds: p95 > 220ms (warning), p99 > 350ms (critical).

Ownership:
- Redwood infra/data: Priyom (instrumentation snippets + Grafana JSON)
- Redwood ops: Laura (deployment/rollout support and escalation path)
- Trialsight: Kyle (access + validation)

I'll attach the tracing guide and a tiny Terraform snippet for the S3 bucket policy. Happy to walk through this in the sync.

--
Priyom Das
Staff Engineer, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-poc-tracing-guide.md

Elaine — thanks for the quick reply and for assigning Kyle. Attached is a one-page POC plan that maps deliverables to owners and a timeline. High-level items: 

Week 0 (prep, 3/16): access & network; S3 write test; agree SLO numbers.
Week 1 (3/17–3/23): run 24h smoke + regression; build dashboards; collect traces.
Week 2 (3/24–3/30): soak under peak bursts, validate alerts, cost analysis.

Immediate asks for Trialsight before kickoff:
- S3 bucket endpoint + IAM/service principal or short-lived credentials.
- Confirm target P95 SLO and 1k-token cost budget (we can propose).
- Point of contact for procurement to accept a short SOW/invoice.

If that works, I'll book a 30m engineering kickoff for Tue 3/16 10:00am PT. Confirm and I'll send calendar invite + agenda.

Thanks,
Sergio
